Definition: from G3844 and G3710; to anger alongside, i.e. enrage:--anger, provoke to wrath.
BiblicalUsage: Parorgizo means to provoke to wrath, to anger alongside. God says in Romans 10:19 that He will provoke Israel to anger by a foolish nation, and Paul tells fathers in Ephesians 6:4 not to provoke their children to wrath, but to bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God provokes to wake a people up, and fathers provoke only to tear a child down, and the difference is the whole difference between His anger and mine.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
